title: Spot jobs, sororities and fraternities
summary: They avoided steady work due to day jobs; most work was sorority and fraternity dances, house parties and conventions, declining after the war.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, well I don't like to put bands down. I will say I don't like to go on Bourbon Street but that's not anybody's fault really. Well Bourbon Street is all tourist trade.

Yeah. I sneak around and listen to you on the side. It's just, it's too expensive. The tourists can afford that, really. That's right. But when you're with bands like Salvaggio and the Blue Parity, would they have any steady work at all? All spots? All spots.
No, we weren't interested in steady work. We didn't want to work six nights a week. Yeah. Because we all had day jobs, you know, in those days.
And would that be house parties, dances, fraternities, sororities?

House parties, sororities. Sororities and fraternities. That was the main thing in the old days, Dick. Like I told you before. In the old days, in the 30s, in the late 20s and 30s, maybe up to, maybe up to 40. Between 28 and 40, 1940. There were many sorority and fraternity dances. Plenty of them. Sororities used to give a dance at least once a month. And fraternity is the same way, at least once a month. Some maybe twice a month. Used to be able to go to the Audubon Tea Room every Sunday there was a dance at the Audubon Tea Room. Which has since burned down.
I think they were going to build another one, I don't know.

But that's in the olden days. And you all, they had, and of course you played for conventions, there was always conventions coming up and they would hire various groups, various small groups or big groups. But most of our work in the old days, the way we operated, was sororities and fraternities and clubs and house parties and things like that. Which there were plenty of, more of then than you have now.
That's from the beginning up to the time you joined the Navy.

Right, right. And then after the war, things seemed to change. They were less, they weren't quite as often. There may be the sorority fraternities might be every six months instead of every month. And now I've seen some of them, they give one party a year now, or one banquet a year or something like that, or maybe some of them still give quarterly or twice a year, every six months.
